title: State Medicaid Recovery of Cost Share on Special Needs Plans Enrollments
content:
Cost share a protected member of a Special Needs Plans package does not owe is billed to the state Medicaid agency on the package's remittance cycle, and never to the member.

### The condition for billing the state

> The cost share being billed arose on an enrollment whose package permits billing the state, and the member's Medicaid category on the day of service was one the package protects.

The member's Medicaid category on the day of service, as the enrollment record holds it, is one of qualified Medicare beneficiary, specified low-income beneficiary or full benefit dual. Both limbs are tested on the enrollment record, matched to the enrollment the cost share arose on, before the state is billed, and on the category the register holds for the day of service rather than on the member's account of their standing.

### The state's time to answer, and the matching of remittances

The state has the package's payment days to answer each billing, and each remittance is posted against the single billing it answers so that the plan can always say which months are settled.

Billings raised on the state increase the cost share billed to the state Medicaid agency on behalf of a protected member; the state's remittances and the plan's write-offs reduce it. The cost share outstanding from the state for the contract year to date is the total of the billings raised on the state in that year less the amount settled against them by state remittances in the same year.

### Where the state declines a billing

Where the state declines a billing the amount is written off by the plan and never passed back to the member, however the state explains its decision.

### A retroactive grant of Medicaid

A retroactive grant of Medicaid is applied back to the month it took effect: cost share the member already paid for those months is refunded to them and rebilled to the state.

### What the member is told

Nothing in this arrangement is the member's concern, and a member who asks about a bill they were never meant to receive is told simply that they owe nothing.

### Points of judgement

**The package permits billing the state, and the register holds the member's Medicaid category on the day of service as specified low-income beneficiary.** Both limbs are answered, that category being one the enrollment record may hold for this purpose.

**The register holds the member as full benefit dual on the day of service, but the package does not permit billing the state.** The condition is not met either, both limbs being required together.

**The state answers a billing by refusing it, and sets out its reasons.** The amount is written off by the plan. It is never passed back to the member, whatever reason the state gives.
